doc.title: Mr. and Mrs. A.C. Synigal Interview, 1962-05-24

chapter: Photographs of the Creole Fiesta and family
title: First board members, the charter and the first parade
summary: Edna identifies the first board, reads the state charter in a photo, and explains the parade schedule.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Uh-huh. And, uh, oh, this is a beautiful gown. It really makes sense. Okay, so. Now this is the board first, this is the first board members. Um, this is Mrs. Who's this lady? Who's this lady? Who's this? Who's this? Who's this? That's Mrs. Um. Oh yeah.
This one? That's the lady I'm talking about. Yeah, on the side.

What's her name? Beulah. This is Mrs. Beulah-Millette here. And this is the maid of. Porter Edwards. Edwards. He's a famous beautician. And this is, uh, myself. This is Edna, able at Senegal. And I'm reading the charter up here. Do you see the charter up there?
Can you read it? White Old Martin. Uh-huh.

Yeah, side by White Old Martin. Yeah, okay. You can't read it, huh? I can't read it from here. From here. But that's the charter. And this is what I'm reading. That's what I'm reading here. It's the charter to our organization. And this is the, uh, program director. And this is Leona B. Sanabid. And this is Mrs. Bennett G. Brown. This is the mother of Deborah Brown. You heard of her? The singer. Yes. This is her mother. Deborah Brown. I spoke to her this morning. Now, this is the first ladies-in-waiting, we call them, at our first tea. In-waiting at our first tea. September the 26th, 1952. That's, you see, we began in June. And in September we had our first tea. Now, these were the ladies-in-waiting. I can't call all of their names here. But this is my daughter-in-law. The king, my son's wife. This is his wife. She's as small as he is. I wondered if he ever would get a wife to fit him. He told me he would. And so there she is. And these are all the ladies here. I took part at that first tea, in serving, you know, of the tea. So. Now, this is in my patio again. How beautiful this is with all the little girls and all. And with their full hats and dresses. Big hats and, yeah. Uh-huh, you see. Now, this is May the, May the one, second? The second?

Group who rode in the first parade. Rode in the first parade, you see. That was May the second. Because, you see, we have our parade always on the first Saturday. And now, why we have it on the first Sunday? Because we used to always have it on Saturday night. But, uh, it was some confusion about the lights. We couldn't get enough lights and the people couldn't see us. So, they thought if we'd have it on Sunday afternoon, that we would be singing, you know. And it would be better for the, uh, better for ourselves and the people too. And so, these are the people who took part in that first parade. The children, see, and the grown-ups. And that's taken in that, um, patio on the other side. The umbrella was on the other side. Now, this is a beautiful scene. This, doesn't it look like snow? It really does.
